# Design

## Context and Existing Ownership

`IngredientNormalizer`, `UnitNormalizer`, `AisleMapper`, `CategorizeIngredientsProcessor` and `GroceryRecomputeService` currently use normalized raw supply names. Canonical publication replaces stale evidence reads; identity mapping is saved at import/correction, never guessed per grocery refresh. See [dataset evaluation](sources.md).

## Decisions and Tradeoffs

App-owned IDs outlive upstream code changes. Confirmed preparation variants can share an ID; purchase qualifiers keep fresh/canned, salted/unsalted, dietary and product forms separate. A food ID is not a row ID: grams and volume may remain separate shopping rows. Missing translation keeps source shopping spelling and deterministic fallback key. Do not publish unvalidated EN/FR labels as facts or strip accents blindly when they create collisions.

A curated initial vocabulary and safe fallback is preferable to a large permissive-but-noisy automatic crosswalk. AI can propose at ingestion; source links, exact relation, qualifiers and collision tests determine acceptance, not confidence alone. Private manual corrections never auto-publish as global aliases. Pin dictionary revision; changing a label alone does not change row/check identity. Mapping changes re-run structural continuity policy with explicit affected-set review, not silent global merges.

## First Observable Slice

Import fixture onion diced, onion sliced and verified oignon émincé associations → saved IDs/provenance → real API/PostgreSQL → deterministic grocery grouping in EN then FR. Fresh and canned tomato remain separate. Spy on provider boundary and assert zero calls for read/recompute. Category correction preserves manual scope and crosses real persistence/recompute plus method-sensitive mocks.

## State, Concurrency and Recovery

Canonical contentRevision guards recipe shopping corrections; categoryRevision guards household aisle overrides. Catalogue release/revision is separate from recipe content and cannot silently rewrite saved mappings. Multiple source aliases for one match key or conflicting manual categories remain unresolved until reviewed. Backup preserves the referenced identity revisions and protected corrections without requiring upstream network access.

## Compatibility, Rollout and Reversal

Depends on canonical quantities/association and dependable row identity; reuses their schemas. Keep initial normal category key endpoint until the explicit food-scoped contract is approved, then move known mappings under a guarded adapter and retain fallback-key correction for unresolved identities. A mapping release has affected row/alias/category manifests and can be disabled without deleting human corrections. No dataset dependency is added during planning.

See the shared [dependency/conflict review](../canonical-ingredient-correction/review.md) for approval and release order, and [acceptance corpus](../canonical-ingredient-correction/acceptance-corpus.md) for preservation cases. Proposed API/schema details have one owner in [contracts.md](../canonical-ingredient-correction/contracts.md).
# Scale ingredient uses in cooking steps

## Why

Ingredient-only scaling leaves step quantities contradictory. Step uses need explicit revision-bound associations to original recipe demand while cooking remains available when a mapping is uncertain.

## Outcome and Scope

Mandatory ingredient-use scaling, coherent ingredient/step projection and current-recipe reading at recorded prepared counts. No general formula language, prose-wide numeric replacement or new grocery demand. Explicit partial amounts remain original after total correction and still scale with portions; relative language stays relative, with original readable wording for inconsistent allocations. Cook mode omits the routine step-uncertainty notice and duplicate header ingredients link; phone Edit/View Original actions return to the right while the view toggle stays left and tablet controls retain their lower-left layout.

## What Changes

- **BREAKING:** adopt the applicable shared [contract](../canonical-ingredient-correction/contracts.md) with explicit compatibility/failure behavior.
- Preserve user decisions and existing safety boundaries in the shared [review](../canonical-ingredient-correction/review.md).
- Add adversarial acceptance from the shared [corpus](../canonical-ingredient-correction/acceptance-corpus.md); no product implementation in this session.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

None.

### Modified Capabilities

- `cooking`: project validated uses and preserve cooking context.
- `supper-servings`: include step uses in shared portions projection.
- `recipe-editing`: guard instruction edits in original basis.

## Impact

Depends on the canonical foundation and companion ownership map as specified in design.md. Future apply must synchronize OpenAPI, generated clients, consumers and stateful mocks where affected, and qualify actual persistence/workflow seams. Planning existence does not establish implementation readiness.

Ambiguous trusted measurements that cannot be represented safely keep legacy read access until manual reconciliation; do not erase them for a migration completion percentage.

Current-format ordinary merge and explicitly selected exact replacement are separate. Version and timestamps cannot establish precedence. An old backup is unsupported, not implicitly convertible inside restore. The one-time forward importer accepts only its manifest's input list; legacy source readability during this process does not promise continued old-backup support. Existing historical voter privacy, extras, report state and preparation/serving recovery remain intact.

## Existing operations own canonical backup and seed

Dreaming’s db-backup step invokes BackupDatabase and the same `ManagementService.BackupAsync` as POST `/api/management/backup`. POST `/api/management/seed` invokes `RestoreAsync`; evolve these owners to write/read the existing version-2 canonical recipe codec. Keep the existing disk layout and management routes. Any necessary format/integrity inventory is internal to these operations, not a second recovery API or user-facing package. Whole-installation database plus asset backup remains a separate protection against disk loss and migration rollback.

Preflight canonical input before household mutation. New destination recipes retain exported IDs and exact canonical content; repeated identical seed is idempotent. A divergent current destination is not authority to overwrite newer human facts: preserve it and report conflict unless the existing captured revision/publication owner proves authority. Sync remains recipe-only and uses captured input, revision guards and durable publication/retry ownership; it must never invoke household seed or infer permission from timestamps. Legacy readability before activation is not a promise of permanent old-backup support; cutover remains fenced until the current-only boundary is qualified.

## First Observable Slice

Disposable PostgreSQL plus copied recipe/media store → no-write manifest → convert one 4-portion 1/3-cup recipe with current edits and one partial step → existing Dreaming/management backup → management seed into an isolated destination → independent read-back → repeat. Compare every canonical field, source/media hash, relationship and protected household field; distinguish this seed merge from independent whole-installation exact restore; interrupt before/after commit and resume idempotently. Prove unsupported old format preflight has zero writes before widening batches.

Frontend, backend and database are deployed together as one coordinated release,
as confirmed by Alex. Do not add an independent rolling-version compatibility
program or legacy string-write translation. Already-open older tabs remain possible:
reject their incompatible canonical writes atomically and retain recoverable drafts
through refresh and reconciliation. Unconverted recipe readability and current-app
review-material editing are data-transition behavior, not support for old app versions.
The deployment unit includes its schema migration; durable older workflow results
still need captured-revision validation before they can publish.

#### Scenario: Exact snapshot includes canonical ownership
- **WHEN** a compatible exact snapshot is captured after canonical write cutover
- **THEN** it includes authoritative exact canonical facts, ingredient/step/binding identities, saved food associations/labels/overrides, content/check revisions, source evidence/protection, serving/preparation state and required durable conversion/refresh work with matching media
- **AND** restore preserves human facts and does not silently substitute legacy-only rows

Explicit null/empty fields SHALL remain authoritative. One-time forward conversion SHALL be a distinct operation.

Current-format exports and restore SHALL preserve occurrence identity, actual preparation date and recorded portion context independently of current recipe content. ### Requirement: Evolve existing backup, seed and sync operations

Canonical backup and seed SHALL use the existing Dreaming/management backup and management seed flows and existing disk layout. They SHALL NOT require a new public recovery API or user-facing package workflow. Recipe-only sync and forward reprocessing SHALL NOT invoke household restore. Whole-installation database-and-asset recovery SHALL remain separate disk-loss/rollback protection.

#### Scenario: Existing operation round trip
- **WHEN** a canonical recipe is edited, Dreaming or management backs it up, and management seed loads that disk state into an isolated destination
- **THEN** stable recipe/line/step IDs, exact amounts, bindings, nulls/clears, source/media and supported household/history/extra state survive
- **AND** repeating the same flow neither duplicates identities nor replays cleared values

#### Scenario: Stale recipe sync retry
- **WHEN** an older sync or publication retry encounters newer human content
- **THEN** it preserves the newer content and files or reports the captured revision conflict, without reseeding household state


### Requirement: Migrate in place before considering a recipe-only disk fallback

The default forward upgrade SHALL convert live recipes in place with stable recipe IDs and protected household relationships. Per-recipe publication SHALL be revision-guarded, atomic, resumable and idempotent. Unrepresentable trusted facts SHALL defer with usable prior content, not be silently discarded.

- **WHEN** upgrade stops after some recipes commit

#### Scenario: Human edit during conversion
- **WHEN** live content changes after dry-run capture
- **THEN** that recipe conflicts without overwriting the change

#### Scenario: Unknown measurement
- **WHEN** a legacy row has no proven numeric association
- **THEN** current text, evidence and valid unknown fields survive without positional guessing

#### Scenario: Protected fields
- **WHEN** approved fallback publishes selected recipe content
- **THEN** before/after protected household hashes and relationships remain equivalent

#### Scenario: Expected synchronized recipe content
- **WHEN** a necessary fallback finds matching disk/database recipe IDs and supported content under its documented comparison

Write activation SHALL require old-writer fencing, supported unsaved-draft recovery, isolated migration/recovery rehearsal and an independently verified rollback pair. - **WHEN** an old tab sends ingredient/instruction content during cutover
- **THEN** it conflicts atomically and the supported refresh route retains all drafts

- **WHEN** an old backup is selected on the new app
- **THEN** it is clearly unsupported without mutation or implicit upgrade

#### Scenario: Migration interval
- **WHEN** conversion fails before the new backup exists
- **THEN** the operator has a verified pre-cutover snapshot with its exact compatible executable/schema and a rehearsed recovery route

### Requirement: Read supported legacy recipe content

**Reason**: Routine recovery supports only the declared current format after cutover.

**Migration**: Use explicit bounded one-time forward conversion of approved recipe source files before cutover; unsupported old backups fail routine preflight without mutation.

## MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: Select recipes with persisted export payload

For non-deleted recipes, export SHALL write metadata when a retained source PDF exists, or a nonempty name has images or synthesis, or canonical ingredient content, raw metadata, notes or a known rating provides payload. Otherwise it SHALL skip the recipe.

#### Scenario: Ready-shaped recipe
- **WHEN** a non-deleted recipe has a name and positive image count but no metadata, notes or known rating
- **THEN** export writes recipe.info

#### Scenario: Empty placeholder
- **WHEN** a recipe has no source PDF, name, images, synthesis, raw metadata, notes or known rating
- **THEN** export skips its metadata file

#### Scenario: Retained PDF
- **WHEN** a non-deleted unfinished recipe retains source.pdf
- **THEN** export includes its metadata regardless of the ordinary payload test

#### Scenario: Canonical content is the retained payload
- **WHEN** a non-deleted recipe has canonical ingredient facts but no other ordinary export payload
- **THEN** export includes that recipe rather than skipping its canonical content

### Requirement: Refresh metadata while retaining existing recipe content

For an included recipe, export SHALL refresh recipe.info and replace recipe.json with current version-2 supported database content, including cleared values, exact canonical quantities/notation, ingredient/step identities, bindings, units/packages, shopping identities, content revisions/evidence/protection, separate serving basis and retained normalized metadata. Retired health, dietary and balance fields SHALL remain omitted. Original, PDF/page and hero media SHALL remain untouched; recipe.info SHALL NOT become another current ingredient owner.

#### Scenario: Existing recipe content
- **WHEN** an included recipe already has recipe.json
- **THEN** export replaces stale content with current database content

#### Scenario: New recipe content
- **WHEN** recipe.json is absent and ingredients are present
- **THEN** export creates serialized recipe content

#### Scenario: Metadata refresh
- **WHEN** an included recipe has changed notes or rating
- **THEN** export updates those fields in recipe.info

#### Scenario: Cleared content
- **WHEN** an included recipe has cleared ingredients or raw metadata since its previous export
- **THEN** the new file represents the cleared values and cannot replay the old values

#### Scenario: Repeated current-content round trip
- **WHEN** a current recipe export is restored and exported repeatedly
- **THEN** supported raw recipe content remains unchanged instead of nesting the export envelope into raw metadata

#### Scenario: Full canonical content round trip
- **WHEN** an exported canonical recipe is restored through the supported version-2 format
- **THEN** line identity/order, current descriptions, independently optional quantities/units, provenance, retained evidence and human protection remain equivalent
- **AND** explicit unknown basis or cleared current lines do not replay old values from metadata

### Requirement: Reconstruct recipes from retained metadata and content

Restore SHALL scan retained recipe IDs and skip IDs with neither recipe.info nor recipe.json. Valid recipe.info SHALL provide primary supported metadata; decoded recipe.json SHALL provide canonical ingredients, separate serving basis, retained normalized metadata and supported content fallbacks. Existing management seed SHALL preflight declared current-format input and its internal integrity inventory before any mutation; legacy input is permitted only in the separate one-time forward importer.

#### Scenario: Metadata and content
- **WHEN** valid recipe.info and recipe.json exist for a recipe ID
- **THEN** restore uses info metadata and reads supported ingredient content from recipe.json

#### Scenario: No metadata files
- **WHEN** a recipe directory has neither metadata file
- **THEN** restore skips that recipe ID

### Requirement: Merge recipes without replacing unrelated stored state

Restore SHALL add absent recipe IDs or update supported metadata/content of existing IDs, including soft-deleted IDs. Ingredient replacement SHALL require the supported format and revision/provenance reconciliation; a stale or unprovably divergent current-format record SHALL NOT overwrite newer/protected facts; identical revision with different content SHALL be rejected. Existing deletion markers, attribution and creation time SHALL remain unchanged during that update.

#### Scenario: Existing recipe
- **WHEN** a loaded recipe ID already exists with different notes and name
- **THEN** restore updates notes and name without adding another recipe

#### Scenario: Soft-deleted existing recipe
- **WHEN** a loaded recipe ID is soft-deleted in the database
- **THEN** restore updates its supported fields while retaining its deletion marker

#### Scenario: Database-only recipe
- **WHEN** a database recipe has no loaded disk record
- **THEN** restore leaves that row in place

#### Scenario: Older content targets a richer current recipe
- **WHEN** a supported current-format export has stale or divergent facts/protection relative to the destination
- **THEN** merge preserves those current facts and reports the ingredient conflict or review outcome instead of silently replacing newer or divergent live edits

#### Scenario: Recipe changes during merge reconciliation
- **WHEN** a destination content revision changes after restore inspected it but before ingredient publication
- **THEN** that stale ingredient replacement is deferred or reported without overwriting the newer revision

### Requirement: Online independent exact recovery
The system SHALL provide explicit exact snapshot and restore operations distinct from merge/import, with operator-configured independent storage outside live roots. Current snapshot version 2 SHALL contain authoritative supported row membership, explicit empty collections, complete version-1 history and verified media bytes. Soft-deleted recipes SHALL retain history dependencies; permanently purged recipes and history SHALL be absent.

#### Scenario: Concurrent online snapshot
- **WHEN** an authenticated operator captures a snapshot while requests and workers operate
- **THEN** cooperating writes drain and coordinate for a bounded interval, reads remain available, and the published independent set contains mutually consistent database facts and media
- **AND** timeout or missing media fails capture without replacing a prior complete snapshot

#### Scenario: Online exact restore with preflight
- **WHEN** an operator selects a complete snapshot
- **THEN** all format, schema, membership, relationships and media integrity are validated in staging before any live change
- **AND** exact publication replaces supported destination facts, invalidates stale rounds/continuations/work and rebuilds derived state
- **AND** health and recovery status remain available while final publication briefly coordinates household requests

#### Scenario: Interrupted cross-store publication
- **WHEN** interruption occurs around file-generation activation or database commit
- **THEN** recovery selects the complete committed state or restores the complete prior state before household operations resume
- **AND** retry neither duplicates facts/history nor reports an incomplete restore as successful

#### Scenario: Legacy omission is not exact emptiness
- **WHEN** exact restore receives an unsupported version or missing required artifact including required current canonical/household/history artifacts

## Recipe content and exact quantities

```json
{
  "contentSchemaVersion": 2,
  "contentRevision": "opaque-token",
  "servings": 4,
  "ingredientLines": [{
    "id": "uuid",
    "description": "pasta",
    "amount": {"kind":"scalar", "value":{"n":"200","d":"1"}},
    "amountText": "200",
    "unit": {"text":"g", "definitionId":"mass:g"},
    "scaling": "proportional",
    "package": null,
    "shopping": {"name":"pasta", "foodId":null, "mappingRevision":null},
    "provenance": {"origin":"human", "sourceRef":null, "protectedFields":["amount"]}
  }],
  "instructionSections": [{"id":"uuid", "name":null, "steps":[{
    "id":"uuid", "text":"Add 200 g pasta.", "textRevision":"opaque-step-token", "bindings":[]
  }]}]
}
```

IDs are server-issued UUIDs; create drafts carry a request-local clientId mapped in the authoritative result, not a claimed saved ID. Lists define order. Sections preserve supported nested source ordering without a general nested recipe engine. A step's textRevision changes only with its text; contentRevision changes on semantic content publication. Source metadata has sourceRevision plus content-addressed evidence references. Keep evidence access behind existing household authorization; shared DTOs need not expose raw private evidence.

`amount` is null, scalar as above, or `{"kind":"range","min":{"n":"2","d":"1"},"max":{"n":"3","d":"1"}}`. Nonnegative normalized numerator strings and positive denominator strings have at most 38 decimal digits each, no leading zeros except zero, gcd=1; endpoints ordered min≤max. Transport uses strings to avoid JS safe-integer loss. Arithmetic uses checked exact intermediates; overflow returns unresolved projection with original evidence, never saturation/NaN. API rejects invalid persisted values with 400. `amountText` retains supported original spelling (including Unicode fractions) only if it parses to the identical amount; generated projections never replace it. Null amount requires null amountText; unparsed imported text remains description/evidence, not a numeric assertion.

Input grammar in the amount field: unsigned integer, dot decimal or locale French comma decimal (no thousands separators), ASCII proper/improper fraction n/d, mixed whole + fraction, listed Unicode fractions ¼ ½ ¾ ⅐ ⅑ ⅒ ⅓ ⅔ ⅕ ⅖ ⅗ ⅘ ⅙ ⅚ ⅛ ⅜ ⅝ ⅞, or two such scalars separated by hyphen/en dash. Normalize spaces, reject exponent, negative sign, denominator zero, multiple separators and ambiguous `1,000` (offer correction, never infer 1000). Range input is explicit; do not parse a hyphen in arbitrary ingredient prose. Original notation survives a round trip; output formatting uses deterministic locale conventions without feeding rounded values back to storage.

Unit is independently null, or `{text, definitionId:null|supported-id}`. Null unit is no declared unit, not an assertion of pieces. Unitless known counts can group together; do not merge them with cloves/cans absent explicit count semantics. Supported exact definitions start with metric mass/volume and explicit count kinds. Alex approved preserving cups, teaspoons and tablespoons in three independent unit families, with equivalent English/French aliases normalized within each family (cup/cups/tasse/tasses; tsp/teaspoon/c. à thé; tbsp/tablespoon/c. à soupe). Quantities remain in their declared family without automatic conversion to millilitres or between culinary families. Existing implicit 240/15/5 ml assumptions are not the desired behavior and cannot populate new definition IDs. Regional definitions must be explicit and validated. No mass/volume or drained/net conversion without evidence. `package` is null or `{countUnit, capacity:{amount,unit}, basis:"net"|"drained"|"unspecified"}`; capacity stays fixed while the line's count scales. No purchase rounding.
